problems.statement: The spring 2026 recovery-time (layover) cut on 21 of 38 routes, made to free nine buses for Route 51, is the main driver of the OTP decline: late arrivals no longer get absorbed and bunch into late departures on the next trip.

The Halvorsen Avenue and Bridgeport Road lane reductions (from 2026-04-20) add a second, larger OTP loss on five routes (9, 14, 22, 31, 33). These routes also had their layover cut, so the two causes compound there.
Operator absenteeism is up 40% and is the cause of the OTP drop, as the client presented.

The 40% absence increase is mostly a measurement artifact of ShiftLine, which went live 2026-03-30 and now records partial-day absences that the legacy process never counted. Full-day absences are up only 1.1%.
Extraboard coverage failures and late pull-outs from garages are not materially worse: missed trips from no operator and late pull-outs are flat, and Group C shows no OTP decline.
The OTP decline is a measurement or AVL artifact.
Higher passenger loads or dwell times explain the decline.

Some of the partial-day early leaves are a symptom of the layover cut, since operators on recovery-cut routes leave early more often (18 vs 10 per 100). Seniority, age, route length and garage are confounded with this, and there is no pre-April baseline.

Management's distance from the schedule and layover problem has let it go uncorrected: the schedule grievance went unanswered, the Director dismisses the service change and road work, and he intends to push the attendance policy on the board unchanged. This is a fit problem between the formal organization and the work.

causalClaims.to: Late terminal departures and OTP decline on those routes
Additional OTP decline on corridor routes 9, 14, 22, 31, 33

actions.action: Do not roll out the tougher attendance policy with discipline at three occurrences in 90 days, and do not take it to the board as planned.
actions.rationale: The absence rise is largely a recording artifact and does not explain the OTP loss, and the policy would discipline partial-day leaves that may be a symptom of the schedule while aggravating the union.

actions.action: Restore recovery time on the 21 cut routes, starting with the five corridor routes and the Group B routes that show late terminal departures, or add buses or trips to fund it.
actions.rationale: This addresses the best-supported cause and is quick to reverse. A pilot on a few routes can be checked against Group C as a control.

actions.action: Re-time the corridor routes (9, 14, 22, 31, 33) for the work-zone running times (about 6.5 more minutes on Halvorsen and 5.5 more on Bridgeport) and coordinate with the city on mitigation such as signal priority or lane management.
actions.rationale: Scheduled running times were never adjusted, and the construction is expected to last until August 2027.

actions.action: Restate the absence baseline by separating full-day and partial-day occurrences, and correct the Director's and board's 40% framing.
actions.rationale: This removes the misleading metric and stops decisions being made on an artifact.

actions.action: Answer the May schedule grievance and open a joint labor-management review of layovers and breaks.
actions.rationale: Operators have raised the issue and it went unanswered, so answering it builds trust and gives a channel for field information.

actions.action: Review the attendance policy design, including how partial-day events are handled and what thresholds apply, after the schedule is fixed and with the new baseline.
actions.rationale: Whether partial-day leaves are misconduct or a response to schedule conditions is not yet known.

actions.action: Reallocate buses away from other routes, or add extraboard capacity, to cover the absence problem.
actions.rationale: Missed trips and pull-outs are flat, so there is no coverage shortfall to fix.

nextEvidence: Pilot result: OTP and terminal late-departure share on a few restored-layover routes (with and without construction) against Group C as control
Early-leave rates by route compared within the same garage, or a seniority-matched sample, to separate schedule effect from age, route length and garage
Counts of partial-day absence reasons and times of day (for example illness mid-shift versus end of a long run), and of grievance filings, to see how many follow late terminal arrivals
output.summary: The OTP drop is not caused by absenteeism. ShiftLine (live 2026-03-30) started recording partial-day absences that were never counted before. Full-day absences are up only 1.1%, and missed trips and late pull-outs are flat. The cause is schedule and environment. The April layover cut on 21 routes explains the step down in Groups A and B, with 81% of late first departures following tight turnarounds. The construction from April 20 adds a second drop on the five corridor routes, which also had their layovers cut. Group C is flat. Restore layovers, re-time the corridor routes, fix the absence metric and answer the grievance. Do not launch the discipline policy.
